purpose: Define safety-state invariants for power, reset, arm and fault sequencing without inventing product timing values or a final implementation.

states.name: POWER_OFF
states.verification: schematic power-state analysis then bench observation

states.name: AUX_UP_MCU_HELD_RESET
conditions: MCU reset asserted or not executing application
states.verification: power sequencing and reset bench test

states.name: MCU_BOOT_UNARMED
conditions: no valid deliberate arm transition completed
states.verification: firmware plus hardware interlock state test

states.name: DRIVER_AWAKE_UNARMED
states.verification: scope capture of gate outputs and permission state

states.name: ARMED_NORMAL
states.verification: arming state-machine and PWM-enable bench test

states.name: ASYNC_HARD_FAULT
states.verification: fault injection plus oscilloscope; compare measured worst case to final semiconductor safe-action budget

states.name: POST_FAULT_LATCHED
conditions: latched fault not explicitly cleared/rearmed under frozen policy

states.name: WATCHDOG_OR_SOFTWARE_RESET
states.verification: induced reset plus gate/PWM scope capture

states.name: BROWNOUT_OR_PARTIAL_POWER
conditions: supply ramp/drop or partial-domain power state
states.verification: controlled supply sequencing plus rail/pin current and PWM observation

states.name: EXTERNAL_INHIBIT_FAULT
conditions: external inhibit/E-stop interface asserted or in a defined wiring-fault state
states.verification: interface fault injection after external safety contract freezes

mandatory_evidence_fields: power state and supply ramp conditions
anti_hallucination_rule: Null timing, backfeed and re-arm fields remain OPEN. The matrix defines required safe-state behavior but does not claim measured latency, certification or final implementation.
